mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the direct shareholder / ultimate beneficial owner (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registrar of companies in the jurisdiction of origin of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel, mutually exclusive path: if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member, notarize the document and then obtain a Hague Apostille from that state's designated Competent Authority; if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention member, notarize the document, have the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin state certify it, and then apply to the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in that state for consular legalization. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Status) issued within 90 days before submission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registrar of companies in the jurisdiction of origin of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel, mutually exclusive path: if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member, notarize and obtain a Hague Apostille from the origin state's Competent Authority; if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention member, obtain notarization, origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification, and then consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. Never combine apostille and consular legalization in one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the China WFOE and appointing the local incorporation agent and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notarized board resolution of the foreign investor or notarized power of attorney executed before a notary public in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel, mutually exclusive path: for Apostille states, notarize the resolution/PoA and obtain a Hague Apostille from the origin Competent Authority; for non-Apostille states, notarize, obtain origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and then consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternatives, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / constitutional documents of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or authorized legal counsel in the jurisdiction of origin, with notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel, mutually exclusive path: if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member, notarize and obtain a Hague Apostille; if not a member, notarize, authenticate through the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize through the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. The two authentication regimes are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the direct shareholder / ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the investor's account, signed by an authorized bank officer in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel, mutually exclusive path: for Apostille Convention states, notarize the bank officer's signature and obtain a Hague Apostille; for non-member states, notarize the signature, have the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs certify the notary, and have the Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalize the certified document. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all direct shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, supervisors, senior management, authorized signatories, and any individual or entity holding at least 25% ownership or control. The process must include Politically Exposed Persons checks in both domestic and foreign official positions, including family members and close associates; exact-match and fuzzy-match screening against OFAC SDN/NS-MIC/SSI lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU/UK sanctions listings, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, and the PBOC financial sanctions lists; independent verification of date of birth, nationality, residence, occupation, source of funds, and source of wealth; adverse-media review; beneficial ownership structure charts; and enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions, legal persons created in secrecy havens, and shell-company indicators. Transactions or relationships involving a positive sanctions match are prohibited; PEP exposure requires senior-management approval, enhanced monitoring, and continued review unless exception is justified and documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Name Clearance System integrated with the National Enterprise Registration Information Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese enterprise name must be expressed in simplified Chinese characters and arranged in a four-tier structure: (1) administrative division; (2) distinctive trade name; (3) industry or business description; (4) legal form, namely limited liability company. An English name may be filed separately for banking and export purposes and must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the Chinese name. The trade name may not be identical or confusingly similar to registered names, protected trademarks, or publicly recognized enterprise names; pinyin is accepted for foreign investor transliteration only when the investor has no known Chinese trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name-clearance portal rejects the proposed name, the applicant will receive a written or electronic decision stating the statutory ground. The applicant may (i) correct the prohibited or similar elements and resubmit a new name application; (ii) apply for administrative reconsideration to the next higher level market supervision administration or the same-level people's government within 60 days of the rejection decision; or (iii) file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within 6 months of the rejection decision. The appeal must identify the case number, the exact name refused, the legal basis for legality, evidence of prior trademark rights or registry searches, and a request for extension of the name reservation if the original 30-day window expires during the appeal. A formal opinion from a PRC-licensed attorney should accompany the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared co-working address is not permissible as the sole registered address for a medical EMR SaaS WFOE. The applicable tax authority, the local market supervision administration, and commercial banks reject such addresses because they cannot demonstrate actual business substance, managerial presence, safe custody of medical records, or statutory books and records. The company must maintain a physical lease in China, with the address appearing on the business license, tax registration certificate, bank account KYC files, and social insurance registration. Home-based or remote work may supplement but cannot replace the physical registered office for this regulated medical software business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: high, approximately 75-85% within the initial 12 months of operation. Unannounced on-site inspections are performed by the municipal tax authorities, the local market supervision administration, and the local public security cyber-security unit. The inspection checklist includes physical attendance of personnel, original lease deed and rent invoices, business license and tax registration certificates, accounting books and vouchers, medical-data handling procedures, cybersecurity and privacy policies, software development activity, and power consumption showing regular business operation. Any mismatch between the registered address and the actual operational site triggers penalties and adverse bank due diligence findings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 29 December 2023, effective 1 July 2024), especially Articles 23-34, 43, 47 and 99; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4 and 31; and the regulations implementing foreign-invested enterprise registration under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) at the municipal or district level where the registered office is located, operating under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company (leading to issuance of the Business License for Enterprise Legal Person).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum amount is imposed on a general WFOE under the 2023 Company Law. The registered capital is set by the shareholder and may be paid in instalments, but the unpaid balance must be fully paid within five years from incorporation (Article 47). No blocked escrow account is required for a standard digital-services WFOE. Any capital contribution in the form of technology or intellectual property must be valued by an independent appraiser and reported to the market regulator. If the business scope appears on the Foreign Investment Negative List, additional approval conditions may apply, including a higher minimum capital threshold or commercial-authority approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMPANY LAW OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA (2023) (the 'Company'). THIS RESOLUTION IS UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED AS A WRITTEN RESOLUTION WITHOUT AN IN-PERSON MEETING IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANY LAW AND THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. WHEREAS the sole shareholder has subscribed for the entire registered capital of the Company in the agreed amount and on the terms set forth in the Articles of Association; and WHEREAS the directors have considered the incorporation expenses, banking arrangements, registered office and statutory officers required for the ordinary conduct of the Company's business; NOW, THEREFORE, the directors RESOLVE: (1) SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The Board accepts the shareholder's subscription for the whole of the registered capital of [amount], and confirms that the liability of each shareholder is limited to the unpaid portion of the capital subscribed. The Board authorizes the legal representative to issue payment calls and to deliver any statutory declarations. (2) BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board approves the opening of corporate bank accounts with ICBC, China Construction Bank, or another licensed commercial bank designated by the legal representative, and authorizes the following signatories, jointly and severally as specified in the delegation, to operate those accounts: [Director A] and [Director B]. All funds of the Company must be deposited only into these authorized accounts, and any two authorized signatories must execute cheques, transfers or electronic banking instructions exceeding RMB 500,000, unless a different threshold is approved by the Board. (3) REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts the registered office located at [full address] as the statutory seat for all corporate records, service of process and governmental notifications, and directs company counsel to place the original lease and any required landlord consent in the corporate binder. (4) STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints [Name] as Legal Representative and President, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Supervisor, each with the powers and fiduciary duties permitted under the Company Law. Each officer must sign an acceptance and comply with the Company's seal control policy, accounting system and disclosure obligations. (5) CORPORATE GOVERNANCE. The Board approves the standard Articles of Association, the corporate seal and seal protocol, and the initial resolution register, and directs the statutory officers to make all required filings, payments and notifications for the Company to remain in good standing under Chinese law and to obtain all necessary licenses for its electronic medical record software-as-a-service business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign-Investment Negative-List Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) online name-reservation window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to formal registration, the foreign shareholder must apply for pre-approval of the proposed company name (one primary name and up to three alternatives) through the SAMR online platform or a self-service terminal at the local AMR. The AMR will check the name against the national enterprise-name database and verify that the proposed business scope is not on the Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access. If the scope is in a restricted category, a negative-list approval from the competent commerce/industry authority must be obtained before the name reservation is finalized. The name-reservation notice is valid for six months. This filing is tracked against the composite key CN_WFOE_LTD for audit purposes.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Legal existence documentation for the foreign investor (certificate of incorporation) with apostille or consular legalization
Power of attorney for the China-resident agent
Statement confirming compliance with the Foreign Investment Negative List
Initial draft of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity or ambiguity, the investors may substitute one of the alternates already filed; if a Negative List restriction is identified, the business scope must be revised to remove the restricted services or the investor must obtain the relevant administrative approval before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarized Submission, Articles of Association, and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) via the National Enterprise Registration Online Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the name is reserved, the foreign shareholder must submit the complete registration packet through the 'Enterprise Registration' function of the designated AMR portal. All foreign-language documents, including the investor's certificate of incorporation and any corporate authorizations, must be notarised and legalised (apostille or Chinese embassy/consular legalisation) and accompanied by a Chinese or English translation as required by the local AMR. The proposed Articles of Association must contain the provisions required by the Company Law: registered capital, subscription amounts, payment period, business scope, composition of the first board of directors and company seal management. The system generates a receipt with a tracking number; the AMR performs a back-office review and, if satisfied, issues the Business License for Enterprise Legal Person, confirming that the WFOE has separate legal personality and limited liability.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Application for establishment registration of a foreign-invested company
Notarised and legalised investor certificate of incorporation and authorisation documents
Articles of Association in duplicate, signed by all shareholders
Proof of registered office (lease deed or property certificate plus landlord consent)
Appointment instrument for the first directors and legal representative, with identity and passport copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a deficiency notice or suspends the application, the applicant has 15 working days to cure all defects and resubmit through the portal; if suspension results from a Negative List issue, the business scope must be amended, or the appropriate foreign-investment approval must be obtained, before a fresh application is made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Seal Carving, Tax Registration and Foreign-Exchange Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) for seal engraving; State Taxation Administration (STA) for tax registration; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for foreign-direct-investment information reporting; licensed commercial bank for basic account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business License is issued, the WFOE must obtain its official company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and contract seal from a licensed engraving company approved by the Public Security Bureau. The engraving permit is applied for at the local PSB window using the original Business License and the legal representative's identification. At the same time, the company must complete tax registration through the electronic tax bureau, obtaining the unified social credit code certificate; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. Within 30 days, the company must open a basic deposit account at a licensed bank and make the required foreign-direct-investment information report to SAFE, through the bank and via the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System. The legal representative must execute the electronic sign-away for these filings.
required_dossiers: Business License for Enterprise Legal Person
Legal representative passport and Chinese residence document, if held
Seal engraving approval application form
Tax registration application using the unified social credit code
FDI information registration form and proof of capital contribution source for SAFE
Basic bank account opening application and anti-money-laundering/KYC dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal engraving approval is delayed, resubmit corrected materials; if SAFE rejects the FDI information because of source or amount mismatches, amend the registration via the reporting bank or apply for a SAFE rectification; any tax registration error may be corrected through the electronic tax bureau's risk-verification function.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance Resolution and Medical EMR / Internet / Data Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR for business-scope modification; National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) for medical-device software registration; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for ICP license; local Public Security Bureau for Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) filing; Cyberspace Administration of China for data-security assessment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of formation, the WFOE must hold (or adopt by written resolution) the First Board Meeting to authorize the bank opening mandate, the seal protocol and the delegation of signing authority, confirming the resolutions passed by the first directors. The company must simultaneously classify its EMR SaaS software under NMPA rules: software with clinical decision-support or diagnostic functions requires a Class II or Class III Medical Device Software Registration Certificate; if the software is purely administrative record-keeping, only an ICP License and an MLPS filing with the local public security authority are mandatory. The company must also conduct a personal information protection impact assessment because the SaaS processes clinic patient data, and file the assessment with the cyberspace administration before putting the service into production.
required_dossiers: First Board meeting minutes and bank authorisation forms
Medical Device Software Registration application (if applicable) with technical documentation and clinical evaluation
ICP Licence application with domain name, hosting and security protocol details
MLPS filing forms and a network security testing report (Level 2 or Level 3)
Personal Information Protection Impact Assessment report and data-processing consent plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NMPA rejects or queries classification, submit additional clinical evaluation data or reclassify under the NMPA software classification catalogue; if the ICP application is suspended, correct the domain-name or hosting-party information and resubmit; if MLPS filing is deficient, engage a qualified security testing agency and resubmit after remediation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) for medical-device software; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for ICP licensing; local Public Security Bureau for Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) filing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Software Registration Certificate (Class II or III, if the EMR SaaS has clinical decision-support functions); otherwise, an Internet Content Provider (ICP) License for commercial internet information services, plus an MLPS Filing Record.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of the People's Republic of China
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - pure digital/software service under ISIC 6201; no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC) or hazardous waste streams from the EMR SaaS activity; office operations only, subject to ordinary municipal waste collection and no industrial discharge permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial fire-safety clearance beyond the basic Fire Safety Inspection Certification required for any commercial office lease; structural-load inspections are Not Applicable because no plant or warehouse equipment is installed; the company must nonetheless register its workplace with the local work-safety supervision agency and comply with the Work Safety Law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online electronic filing and registration through the China National E-Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau, etax.chinatax.gov.cn) with provincial tax service modules
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident investor forms the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) as a limited liability company under the Foreign Investment Law and registers its legal personality with the State Administration for Market Regulation. Under China's multi-registration integration reform, the tax registration is completed simultaneously with the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), and the USCC functions as the taxpayer identification number for the WFOE for enterprise income tax, VAT, and other national taxes. No separate TIN application is required for mainland-incorporated companies. The WFOE must then complete its post-registration fiscal profile in the e-Tax Bureau, select small-scale or general VAT taxpayer status, register payroll and withholding programmes, and activate digital invoice issuance. For a foreign non-resident enterprise that has not established a legal person or branch in mainland China, the Chinese withholding agent must complete non-resident tax registration through the e-Tax Bureau before the first China-sourced payment is made; where the non-resident requires a direct taxpayer identity, the competent tax authority will assign a non-resident taxpayer identification number upon completion of the non-resident enterprise tax registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: China does not offer a check-the-box pass-through election; all domestically incorporated enterprises, including WFOEs, are taxed at the entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. The only material statutory elections are (i) VAT status as small-scale taxpayer versus general taxpayer, with mandatory general taxpayer registration once annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, and (ii) special tax treatment election for qualified enterprise reorganizations, subject to STA filing; no hybrid-mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Tax registration is compulsory within 30 days after business registration without a turnover threshold; mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, while persons with annual taxable sales at or below RMB 5,000,000 may be classified as small-scale taxpayers; cross-border digital/IT services are taxable at 6% when supplied domestically and may qualify for 0% or exemption when exported.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory unified electronic invoice system administered by the STA. VAT special invoices and ordinary invoices must be issued through the tax-control system or the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) platform; invoice data are transmitted online to the tax authority in near real time, and FDEI issuance is integrated with the e-Tax Bureau through statutory APIs and interface-based clearance. Each invoice carries an anti-fraud digital stamp, a unique invoice code, and a verification QR code; invoices that fail online verification cannot be used to claim input VAT credits. General VAT taxpayers must also use the VAT invoice verification module to authenticate counterparty special invoices, and the tax authority may impose tax-control restrictions on abnormal taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for a 0% VAT rate where the goods are actually declared to customs and exported from mainland China to an overseas purchaser, with title passing abroad, and the exporter has filed the export VAT refund/exemption procedure. For cross-border offshore digital services such as EMR SaaS, the zero-rate or VAT exemption with input credit/refund eligibility requires the service provider to be a Chinese resident enterprise, the recipient to be an overseas enterprise or individual, the service to be wholly consumed outside mainland China, no mainland domestic customers to receive the same service, the contract and invoice to be denominated in foreign currency, and the consideration to be paid from outside China and repatriated to mainland China. The SaaS service must be classified as a cross-border IT/software service or offshore outsourcing service under STA guidance; the supplier must file the cross-border taxable service zero-rating/exemption declaration through the e-Tax Bureau, maintain the underlying export service contract, foreign-currency invoice, and foreign recipient documentation, and preserve server access/delivery logs showing the service was accessed and used overseas. Domestic EMR SaaS supplied to hospitals or clinics in mainland China cannot be zero-rated and is subject to VAT at 6%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Declaration Form (customs export declaration with the pre-assigned customs declaration number) for physical software carriers or hardware; not applicable to pure SaaS exports
Original Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment to the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list consistent with the customs declaration and foreign exchange receipt
Bank inbound remittance receipt / Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Confirmation issued by a designated foreign exchange bank or SAFE-approved electronic payment confirmation

For cross-border SaaS with no physical customs clearance: signed export software/service contract, foreign-currency commercial invoice, proof of the overseas recipient's legal existence, and service delivery/output logs demonstrating consumption outside mainland China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, customs, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) conduct cross-matching audits of export declarations, invoice data, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. A false or unsubstantiated export zero-rating claim triggers reversal of the 0% VAT treatment, recovery of unpaid VAT at the domestic rate, mandatory repayment of any input VAT already refunded, and late-payment surcharge at the statutory daily rate of 0.05% per day. Under the Tax Collection and Administration Law, tax evasion is subject to an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the tax underpaid; serious cases attract criminal liability under the Criminal Law, customs fines and confiscation for false export declarations, suspension or revocation of export tax refund/exemption qualification, downgrading of the taxpayer's tax credit status, blocking of digital invoice issuance, and recovery of the tax without a limitation period where fraud, evasion, or refusal to pay is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under PBOC
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime under the PBOC with a bifurcated convertibility framework. Current account transactions, including export proceeds from software and SaaS services, are generally freely convertible and require only bank-level verification and SAFE reporting. Capital account transactions remain heavily regulated and require prior approval, registration, or filing from SAFE for foreign direct investment, cross-border loans, and profit repatriation. For a WFOE, inbound equity capital injections must be converted through a dedicated foreign exchange capital account and used within the approved business scope. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permissible for current-year after-tax earnings, subject to audit report, tax clearance certificate, board resolution, and SAFE registration. Dividend remittance is processed via the bank's SAFE-mandated verification of the outbound remittance application and supporting documents. Surrender of export proceeds is not mandatory as China abolished mandatory surrender requirements in 2012, but all current account receipts must be repatriated to China and either retained in a foreign currency settlement account or converted to RMB via a designated bank. Deferred payment or indirect routing of receivables through offshore accounts is prohibited unless specifically approved by SAFE. The overall convertibility for a medical EMR SaaS exporter is favorable on current account, but any capital structure involving offshore debt, IP license fees, or stock-based compensation creates capital account constraints requiring detailed regulatory filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from service trade (including SaaS subscriptions) must be received within the statutory repatriation timeframe of 180 days from the performance date or as otherwise agreed in the commercial contract, but must be brought onshore before the annual FX supervision and balance report deadline. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may retain foreign currency in its current account Foreign Currency Settlement Account or sell it to a domestic bank on a voluntary basis. All export proceeds must be recorded in the SAFE Digital Foreign Exchange Platform and matched against the service trade contract, invoice, and customs or service quality endorsements where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers such as Neo, Revolut Business, and Airwallex are not recognized as licensed banks or payment institutions by PBOC or SAFE. They cannot legally open account facilities for a mainland China WFOE or execute onshore RMB settlement, capital account conversion, or foreign exchange hedge transactions under Chinese law. Any attempt to route collection through such EMIs would violate currency control regulations and trigger shutdown, fines, or account freezing. The only permissible path for cross-border liquidity is a domestic Chinese bank integrated with SAFE's reporting system; the WFOE should rely exclusively on Tier-1 domestic banks for all collections, disbursements, and FX hedging. Fintech solutions can be used only as non-accounting ancillary billing layers that funnel to a licensed Chinese bank custody account, not as standalone settlement rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. The WFOE's legal representative (statutory director) and at least one additional authorised signatory, typically the general manager or financial controller, must appear in person at the bank's counter branch to complete the corporate account opening interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not tolerated for domestic Chinese corporate accounts; video verification may supplement but never replace the in-branch interview. The bank will conduct a face-to-face due diligence discussion on the business model, source of funds, and expected transaction volumes. For foreign nationals acting as legal representatives, a passport, valid work visa or residence permit, and notarized Chinese translation of the Power of Attorney and board resolution are required. In strictly exceptional cases, some banks allow the legal representative to appear at a Chinese consulate abroad to execute notarized delegation, but the final on-site identity check for the actual signatory still must occur in China.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership chain with a foreign venture capital fund holding multiple special purpose vehicles (SPVs) in different jurisdictions, creating ambiguity about the natural person controlling more than 25% of the WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full corporate org chart from each SPV to the ultimate natural persons; certified copies of certificates of incorporation and register of directors for each offshore entity; audited financial statements for the immediate upstream holding company; notarized ID/passport copies plus proof of residential address for all UBOs above 25%; and a written explanation of the size and source of the engagement capital, backed by bank statements from reputable international banks showing clean funding provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border data transfer concern due to the medical EMR nature of the business, as the Chinese Cyber Security Administration (CAC) classifies personal health data as confidential or important data, presenting a potential regulatory conflict that could be interpreted as structuring transactions to evade data localization rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the CAC Data Export Security Assessment Registration Certificate or a documented exemption letter, a completed Data Transfer Impact Assessment, the Information Security Level Protection (MLPS 2.0) filing record, and a third-party ISO 27001 / SOC 2 Type II audit report. Also submit the contractual clauses for all sub-processors and a confidentiality commitment from the bank's AML officer that the medical data will not be named in any transaction narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media screening hit where an overseas client or beneficiary is a hospital in a restricted country or the software license is resold via a distributor in a high-risk jurisdiction, making the bank question potential revenue derived from sanctioned parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a full list of end-customers with license keys and proof-of-contract for all distributor agreements; run an automated watchlist screening output that shows no exact matches and only low-confidence false positives; provide a written sanctions compliance policy plus a breakdown of how the WFOE ensures no U.S., EU, or UN sanctioned person or entity transacts in the account. Add a director's sworn affidavit and copies of all export clearance documentation for the EMR software.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High frequency of inbound remittances from overseas medical institutions with inconsistent invoice descriptors or transaction narratives that do not match the declared service trade purpose code, raising a red flag for possible merchant-money-comingling or unauthorized cross-border payment aggregation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a scheduled invoice and contract mapping for the trailing 12 months, fully reconciled with the bank's expected purpose code; provide an automated reconciliation report from the billing system (e.g., Stripe or an alternative) that ties each inbound wire to an invoice ID and client contract ID; and submit a certified copy of the WFOE's internal treasury policy that prohibits any settlement from third-party payment aggregators not pre-approved by SAFE, together with a confirmation from the bank's compliance committee that all future wire narratives will use a rigid '[Invoice No.][Invoice Date][Service Type]' convention.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital for the WFOE must be routed through a bank that has received the FDI registration information from SAFE. The foreign shareholder wires funds using the MT103 SWIFT standard, clearly indicating the purpose as 'Equity Investment for Registered Capital' and quoting the SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration Certificate number. The receiving Chinese bank deposits funds into the Foreign Exchange Capital Account, verifies the registration against SAFE's digital platform, and then converts them to RMB only upon submission of a board resolution, a capital contribution schedule, and a conversion use plan. After conversion, RMB must be placed in a Capital Settlement Account and cannot be used for equity investment, securities, or real estate purchases outside the approved business scope. Before settlement, the bank performs a final check on the capital source, the shareholder's proof of funding, and the WFOE's operating license. Capital verification by a licensed Chinese CPA occurs after the full injection, and the verification report is filed with the Administration for Market Regulation and the local SAFE office.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements, the WFOE uses SWIFT MT103 for direct service payments to overseas processors, software subcontractors, and licensing partners, with SAFE-compliant purpose codes and invoice details. Vendor trade settlements for physical infrastructure hardware or server procurement may be executed via Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) when a supplier requires a bank-issued payment guarantee; the issuing bank will require a copy of the purchase order, proforma invoice, and anticipated shipment documents. Documentary Collections are acceptable for low-risk subscription license payments where the documents are simple and no store-of-value guarantee is needed. Bank of China and ICBC can also execute MT102/MT103 batched payments for payroll to overseas contractors, but each payment must carry the correct service trade code and contract registration. No payment can be released without a matching contract in the SAFE service trade registration file; for payments over USD 50,000 equivalent, the bank may request additional evidence such as the licensing agreement, tax payment certificate, or management service output report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward contracts with SAFE-licensed banks under the real demand principle, where the WFOE can lock the USD/CNY rate for a maximum tenor of 12 months tied to genuine service export invoices
FX swaps between RMB and major currencies for same-day or weekend settlement to manage repatriation timing mismatches, subject to counterparty bank availability
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term debt or vendor financing exposure, but prohibited if there is no underlying real transaction
Zero-cost collars or vanilla currency options (call/put structures) when approved by the bank's FX options compliance desk and exclusively for hedge purposes, not for speculation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report for the National Enterprise Credit Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local municipal market regulatory bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year, reporting on the immediately preceding calendar year; no statutory extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file places the WFOE in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; if unfiled for three consecutive years, inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List may trigger administrative revocation of the business license, personal credit restrictions, and disqualification of directors, supervisors, and senior executives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report for Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), submitted jointly through the SAMR national enterprise credit information publicity system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year for the prior calendar year; shareholding transfers or other reportable changes must be updated within 30 calendar days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing triggers a rectification order and administrative penalties under the Foreign Investment Law; the WFOE may lose access to foreign-investment facilitation measures, suffer a negative compliance record, and persistent non-compliance may be referred for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement and Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and local competent tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following each calendar tax year; quarterly provisional payments are made during the year with the final settlement due May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative fines; late payment accrues a daily overdue interest of 0.05% of the unpaid tax; under-declaration penalties range from 50% to five times the tax underpaid; serious cases may trigger tax audit, asset freezing, departure restrictions, bank account freezes, cancellation of tax registration, and administrative strike-off support.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Statements Audit by a PRC Certified Public Accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Chinese CPA firm; audited financial statements submitted with the annual tax settlement and the SAMR annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements as at December 31 must be audited before the May 31 corporate income tax annual return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain the required audit opinion makes the annual tax settlement incomplete and may cause rejection of the SAMR annual report; fines may be imposed under the Accounting Law; dividend remittance, foreign exchange registration, and capital repatriation through SAFE-regulated banks are blocked until a clean audited report is produced.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Social Insurance Contribution Base Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau with social insurance premium collection administered through the local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Normally announced by each municipality between April and June for the current contribution year, with June 30 as the common outer deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declaration or late declaration triggers recomputation of contributions, late-payment penalties, administrative fines, and credit discipline; persistent non-compliance can result in compulsory collection, business operation restrictions, and administrative revocation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Data Security and Cybersecurity Compliance Assessment for the Medical EMR SaaS Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), provincial public security network security department, and National Health Commission data regulatory bodies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Multi-Level Protection of Cybersecurity assessment due annually on the anniversary of the prior assessment; annual data security self-assessment for medical data processors due within 60 days after calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violations are enforceable under the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, and Personal Information Protection Law; fines may reach RMB 1 million for ordinary violations and up to RMB 50 million or 5% of annual revenue for severe violations; regulators may order service suspension, revocation of the medical-information business qualification, or referral for business license strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A WFOE is subject to a zero-threshold compulsory audit: every wholly foreign-owned enterprise must appoint an independent PRC-licensed certified public accountant to audit its annual financial statements regardless of balance-sheet size, revenue, or headcount. The same unconditional audit trigger applies to one-person limited liability companies. For non-WFOE domestic enterprises, the tax authority may administratively order a certified CPA audit when annual turnover exceeds RMB 10 million, total assets exceed RMB 30 million, or headcount exceeds 50 persons; additionally, financial institutions, insurance companies, securities firms, listed companies, enterprises in liquidation, and companies preparing for IPO are mandatorily audited under specialized regulations. Health data processors operating an EMR SaaS platform are subject to a mandatory independent data security audit when the number of processed personal health information records exceeds 100,000 individuals.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE), referred to as PRC GAAP, substantially converged with IFRS; statutory annual financial statements of the WFOE are prepared under full ASBE and audited under the Chinese CPA Auditing Standards. Small-scale eligible companies may elect the PRC Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but a WFOE must nevertheless obtain a full independent audit opinion from a Chinese CPA firm.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Beneficial Owner Information Management measures and Company Law, the WFOE must file initial beneficial owner information with the SAMR within 30 days of incorporation and update such information within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, voting-rights change, control change, or reorganization. A beneficial owner is any natural person directly or indirectly holding at least 25% of equity or voting rights or otherwise exercising effective control. There is no standalone annual UBO form; the annual enterprise information report filed by June 30 must confirm current shareholder and controller data, and any transfer of shares must be reported to the SAMR within the mandatory 30-day change window and to the tax authority where applicable.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 5,000 per annum depending on city, registered office type, and corporate secretarial or local agent support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 18,000 per annum depending on operating scale, transaction volume, medical-data complexity, and Chinese CPA firm tier

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly established software enterprises and high-tech WFOEs may benefit from a two-year exemption and three-year 50% reduction on eligible income; a reduced 15% rate applies to High- and New-Technology Enterprise (HNTE) status; software enterprises with key national planning status may obtain a 10% rate; R&D expenses are super-deducted at 100% of eligible expenditure, yielding a total deduction of 200%. Preferential treatment in free-trade zones such as Shanghai Pilot FTZ or Hainan FTP may reduce the effective rate to 15% for encouraged industries, but the statutory headline rate remains 25% for ordinary resident enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-class) filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Taxation portal; quarterly provisional payments are made on Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual return is due within five months after the fiscal year-end, ordinarily no later than 31 May of the following year; quarterly provisional returns are due within 15 days after each calendar quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payee legal name, taxpayer identification number, enterprise nature and address on the main return header.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Clearly mark the WFOE as a resident enterprise and identify any non-resident related parties on the attached cross-border transaction schedule. Ensure the Chinese tax resident certificate and UBO details of all foreign shareholders are traceable to facilitate future dividend DTA relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from primary business: EMR SaaS subscriptions, clinical workflow implementation, maintenance, cloud hosting and medically-related software licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue derived by the WFOE from services performed or software delivered in mainland China, including deemed income from free trial licences to hospitals. If revenue is collected from foreign clients, explain the source rules under Article 7 of the EIT Law and avoid shifting profit to offshore companies through artificial contracting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of primary operations: cloud infrastructure, medical data centre charges, interruption compensation, clinical integration subcontracting and direct software deployment costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany cloud hosting or support service payments to non-resident associates must be supported by executed contracts, actual receipts, and transfer pricing documentation. Withhold tax on cross-border service fees if the foreign service provider is considered to be earning China-source income, and secure treaty relief before payment if available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling and administrative expenses: payroll, physician onboarding, compliance consultants, data privacy officers, marketing for hospital contracts, and amortisation of capitalised software development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose deductible royalties paid to non-resident IP holders. A deduction will be denied if the beneficial ownership test fails or the royalty is not supported by receiving source tax certificates. Directors must ensure the WFOE retains records showing the actual use of licensed clinical EMR software in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, R&D super deduction, rental and other adjustments to accounting profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If non-resident-shareholder-related R&D costs are reimbursed by the WFOE, ensure the R&D activity and personnel are substantially located in China; otherwise the HNTE 15% rate and R&D super deduction may be challenged. Government grants for hospital software connectivity must be analysed for taxability and disclosed in the non-taxable income line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosures: Schedule of cross-border intragroup services, royalties, financing and profit transfer information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Annual related-party transaction forms are mandatory for a WFOE with cross-border flows. Provide detail on foreign parent or affiliated medical SaaS vendors, the amount of intercompany royalties and service fees, and the TP method adopted. Failure to file opens the door to transfer pricing adjustment and penalty exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses sustained outside China cannot offset taxable income within China; the WFOE must clearly attach separate schedules if its foreign branch or subsidiary losses are being excluded. The general five year loss carryforward applies unless the enterprise has HNTE or encouraged industry treatment, which may permit a ten year period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate calculation, tax payable, and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate or the preferential 15% HNTE/10% key software rate. When claiming foreign tax credits for dividends received from a non-resident subsidiary, attach the underlying foreign tax payment certificate and complete the FTC schedule. Dividends paid to foreign shareholders during the year must be separately captured on the withholding schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax already prepaid quarterly, balance due or refund, and declaration of official interest and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile quarterly A200000 prepayments with the annual liability. If the WFOE withheld tax on non-resident dividends, interest or royalties during the year, report the withheld amounts and remit them within seven days of the date of withholding. Late or omitted withholding will expose the company and its director-signatories to administrative sanctions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under the Tax Collection Administration Law include a fixed fine of RMB 2,000 for a single filing failure, rising to RMB 2,000-10,000 for more serious or repeat violations, plus daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% (0.0005 per day) on unpaid tax. Inaccurate or false declarations causing underpayment of 10% or more of tax payable and exceeding RMB 50,000 in evaded tax trigger criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, punishable with up to seven years imprisonment and fines. Fraudulent VAT special invoices used to reduce the CIT base attract separate criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 205, including monetary fines of RMB 50,000 to RMB 500,000 and imprisonment of responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident corporate shareholder intending to claim a reduced dividend rate under a bilateral Double Tax Agreement must follow the Chinese self-assessment treaty-relief procedure. The beneficial owner must hold a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the residence state, produce an apostilled or legalised copy, and submit the treaty entitlement forms together with board minutes authorising the dividend, shareholding records, audited financial statements and a written declaration that it is the beneficial owner with substance and control over the dividend rights. The WFOE, as withholding agent, must record the treaty entitlement and retain all documentation. If the treaty benefit is granted, the dividend WHT is lowered from 10% to the applicable treaty rate, usually 5% or 10%, and the tax authority may also require submission of a beneficial-owner confirmation checklist to prevent treaty shopping.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding tax rate for outbound interest and royalties paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise is 10% each under EIT Law Article 3(3) and Article 37. Under the relevant DTA, royalty WHT may be reduced to a treaty-specific rate in the range typically 5%-10%, and interest WHT to 5%-10%, only where the recipient is the beneficial owner and has completed the DTA self-assessment procedure with the current foreign tax residency certificate. If the recipient has no substantive risk-management or ownership capacity, China may re-characterise the payment and impose the full 10% gross-base tax plus late payment interest and penalties.
